mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 97 for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST of more than 1% signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.3% month-over-month signals a restrictive monetary policy with declining inflation, which typically precedes recession and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls > -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 2% signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which weakens demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary stimulus.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of non-stimulus triggered episodes.
